design_detail: Multisite, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (ADAPT-2) of extended-release injectable naltrexone plus oral extended-release bupropion in adults with moderate-to-severe methamphetamine use disorder; two-stage sequential parallel design, 12 weeks.
can_establish: Whether the combination increased the proportion of responders (urine-verified reduction in use) relative to placebo.
cannot_establish: Long-term outcomes; effectiveness outside trial conditions; effects in people who use less heavily.

sample.recruitment: Treatment-seeking adults at [to be extracted from PDF] US sites.

outcomes.instruments: Urine drug screens; response defined as at least 3 of 4 methamphetamine-negative urine samples in the final weeks of each stage [to be extracted from PDF]

analysis.effect_sizes: Weighted response about 13.6% vs. 2.5% ([to be extracted from PDF] exact, with CI); number needed to treat about 9.

interpretation_gap.results_show: A statistically robust but modest absolute benefit in a minority of participants.
interpretation_gap.claimed: Reported in media as a 'treatment for meth addiction'; the trial shows a small-to-moderate effect over 12 weeks.

replication.where_it_stands: Single large trial; replication and longer follow-up needed.

funding.funder: NIDA Clinical Trials Network [to be extracted from PDF]

risk_of_bias.reasoning: Well-conducted; attrition handling to be checked.
